title: Small AAA Platelets/GPVI Haemodynamic Inflammation Research Evaluation
summary:
An abdominal aortic aneurysm is a condition in which the large abdominal aorta gradually dilates. Why this change develops, particularly in the early stages, is not yet fully understood. It is suspected that inflammation, changes in blood platelets, and altered blood flow patterns within the vessel wall may play an important role in this process.

The study therefore investigates whether there is a connection between certain changes in the blood, inflammatory reactions, and changes in blood flow, and how these factors influence the growth of small dilations in the abdominal aorta.
conditions: Abdominal aortic aneurysm, without mention of rupture

interventions.name: Following enrollment in the study, examinations will be conducted at 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, and 48 months (MRI scan, ultrasound-tomography, blood tests, clinical examination)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Diagnosed AAA not requiring treatment, with a maximum diameter of 30–45 mm (female) and 30–50 mm (male)
-Ability to provide written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
•Female patients of childbearing age
•Current indication for surgery or treatment
•Previous surgical or endovascular treatment of an AAA
•Acute inflammatory or infectious diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn’s disease, HIV, hepatitis B)
•Known blood clotting disorders
•Malignant diseases currently undergoing active treatment
•Contraindications to MRI examinations
